## Historical audit: S0107

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r2/generic_rsi/C1/development/commons_118588033/trajectory.jsonl`. This audit covers only supplied chunk 1 of 2; neither the reference nor render images are visible to the auditor.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Student request, JSONL line 1 | The formal goal was an editable 3D reconstruction from one photograph, matching viewpoint, framing, objects and materials. The student’s description of a ship accommodation compartment is an **interpretation**, not independently verified scene identity. |
| Student response and execution, lines 3–5 | The first program constructed multiple named assets: room, bunks, lockers, chair, machinery, pipes and fittings. It specified colored materials, procedural deck bump, a camera and lights. Rails, legs and collars were modeled as parts; actual contact or physical connection is not independently verified. Step 1 returned `ok: true`, 238 primitives and a saved render. |
| Student request/response and execution, lines 7–11 | The student received the first render and diagnosed overly pale illumination; this is the student’s visual judgment. It retained the camera, darkened materials and lights, raised mattresses and lockers, and added a transverse wall with repositioned fittings. Step 2 returned `ok: true`, 241 primitives and a saved render. The changes mix appearance and geometry, so their individual effects are not isolated. |
| Student response and execution, lines 15–18 | The student judged depth and overlaps to be the largest remaining mismatch. It raised and moved foreground cabinets, added mounting feet, moved and widened lockers, moved machinery and wall fittings, and altered room and column placement while retaining the camera. Step 3 returned `ok: true`, 245 primitives and a saved render; a select event recorded step 3. |
| Student sessions, lines 2, 8 and 14 | The visible sessions report no tool calls; exploration consisted of authored builds and runner-supplied renders, rather than visible external search or independent measurements. The student received the reference and previous render paths in the successive requests. |

**Teacher input and adoption:** No teacher event or teacher feedback is visible in this chunk. The initial shared reconstruction procedure and subsequent controller requests were actually supplied to the student; the student used named assets, printed primitive counts, and revised after render feedback. These observations do not establish receipt or adoption of any separate teacher intervention.

**Outcome and uncertainty:** Three builds executed and rendered successfully; step 3 was selected in the visible trace. This establishes technical execution, not formal reconstruction success or visual correctness. Final submission and any later review are unknown because the other chunk is unavailable. The student’s brightness, depth and overlap diagnoses remain hypotheses to this auditor. No independent check of image match, object pose, occlusion, part contact, texture appearance, camera framing or lighting quality is possible from the supplied text alone; no render failure is reported.

**Lessons:** Transferably, named semantic groups and explicit primitive counts made successive runnable revisions observable, while render success must be distinguished from visual validation. The proposed bulkhead return, cabinet feet and depth adjustments are task-specific hypotheses, not demonstrated general solutions.
